title: Giving up music and leading his own band in East End
summary: Brunies stopped playing about 25 years earlier. He recalls a band in East End (Bucktown) with piano, drums, banjo and himself on trumpet, near the roof garden.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. When did you give up music? How long since you played music? I thought about 20 years ago. 25 years. 25 years. 25 years. You have a better memory than any of us. Well, it was a happy day in my life. Oh, who tell it? Did you ever have your own band that you were the leader that just played with other bands?

Well, you had the band when you was out in Bucktown. It was your band. Oh, I took it. I was Jesus in the band. Yeah, but I mean, it was still your band. East End. East End. East End. East End. Uncle Lemon. Didn't like the name of Bucktown, so they had a change. No. East End. Violin. Not me. Violin, the piano. Buck Rogers. And drum. Buck Rogers. Me on trumpet. And a banjo player. And it wasn't that far from the roof garden. And that roof garden band was sentimental, you know. They had owls up there. Oh, sometimes. You remember that, yeah? You're making me up now. Yeah. And they all used to play music. And I used to throw that trumpet over towards them, you know. It was high. High they were. And some of them just say, that damn fellow would take that trumpet and throw it away. We don't know where we are on the music. You're not supposed to play. They only sent a word over there about me not playing so loud and everything like that, so I had to cut it down.
